published_basis.author: Stefan Szeider
published_basis.result: SAT for CNF with maximum deficiency k is decidable in O(2^k n^3), producing either a satisfying assignment or a regular-resolution refutation.

uniform_terminal_rule.input_size: N = original encoded input size, N>=2
uniform_terminal_rule.action: run the exact Szeider maximum-deficiency SAT algorithm

legend_effect.L6: PUBLISHED_CERTIFICATE_OUTPUT: SAT assignment or regular-resolution refutation

scope.strength: Works for arbitrary CNF, not only width<=3, so it can consume some wider successors created by previous exact transitions.
scope.ceiling: If delta*(F)>floor(log2 N), the rule returns NO_PROGRESS and no SAT/UNSAT claim.
scope.not_claimed: This does not make the full FPT algorithm polynomial on unbounded maximum deficiency.

combined_frontier_after_R44BB_R44BC.width3: Every fixed surplus layer has exact polynomial one-step progress (R44BB).
combined_frontier_after_R44BB_R44BC.arbitrary_width: Every state with delta*(F)<=floor(log2 N) has an exact polynomial terminal decision (R44BC).
combined_frontier_after_R44BB_R44BC.residual: A surviving candidate hard trajectory must evade both: it must not remain in any fixed-surplus width3 layer and, at every state not otherwise reduced, must have maximum deficiency above the logarithmic terminal threshold.

next_admissible_math.question: Find a uniform exact polynomial transition that reduces unbounded maximum deficiency/surplus, or a precise barrier for one fixed candidate compression.
